correctness.rationale: The exact decomposition of the rook Laplacian gives four eigenspaces, with the m and n eigenspaces merging at equal dimensions. At q=(m-1)(n-1) independent coordinate inputs, PBH on the highest space is equivalent to the complement being a spanning tree by the bipartite cycle-space theorem. For unequal dimensions, a nonzero row or column mode supported on a tree would require a four-cycle. At equal dimensions, the additional eigenspace is characterized by the two component-count sums; an exhaustive extremal edge-count argument leaves precisely two and only two obstruction families. The exact tree counts and zero-forcing comparison follow by constructive arguments. The standard-library checker passed 18,925 exact modular modal cases, a full 3-by-3 Kalman enumeration, 48 larger direct Kalman cases, and small exact zero-forcing checks. Finite tests are not used to infer infinite validity.

originality.rationale: The evaluated novelty is the full if-and-only-if enumeration of minimum dedicated coordinate actuator placements on rook graphs, especially the two disjoint balanced exceptions. General PBH, product eigenvalues, maximum multiplicity, complete-bipartite tree counts, and zero forcing are known and expressly not treated as original. The inspected Cartesian-product paper relies on simple product spectra for its minimum product control theorem and gives layered constructions, not the stated classification when the product spectrum has forced degeneracies. The multiplicity paper gives the number of abstract independent inputs but not all dedicated vertex locations. Published graph-controllability searches and semantic overlap searches produced no scientifically equivalent statement. Historical unindexed coverage remains a risk.

value.rationale: Complete classification and exact labeled enumeration of all minimum coordinate-actuator placements on an infinite family of dense Cartesian-product networks, with a sharp balanced/unbalanced spectral collision and two explicit bad tree types; a one-edge exchange gives a constructive square-case optimal design. The exact selection test is combinatorial rather than repeated full Kalman matrix computations. The strict gap between fixed-Laplacian actuation and strong zero forcing makes the distinction consequential.
